players.product: physics-plus-AI molecular discovery platform and Bunsen co-scientist

quarterly_data.signal: Bunsen launched in early access as an agentic AI co-scientist that executes validated multi-step molecular-discovery workflows. Management said it expands access beyond computational chemists, can monitor and restart failed supercomputer jobs, and is licensed on throughput so higher agent-driven usage can translate into revenue.

Q2 ACV was $29.6 million, up 27% year over year; trailing-four-quarter ACV reached $208 million. Software revenue was $32.5 million and hosted revenue was $15.2 million, or 47% of software revenue versus 31% a year earlier. Full-year ACV guidance remains $218 million-$228 million.
quarterly_data.figure: ACV $29.6M (+27%); TTM ACV $208M; software $32.5M; hosted 47%; FY ACV $218M-$228M

quarterly_data.signal: Drug-discovery revenue rose to $23 million from $13.9 million, helped by a $10 million Ajax milestone. Since 2020, therapeutics activities across collaborations and co-founded companies have realized more than $750 million; quarter-end cash and marketable securities were $419 million.
quarterly_data.figure: drug discovery revenue $23M; >$750M realized since 2020; cash $419M

connects_to.relationship: enterprise deployment of Bunsen and molecular discovery software

contracts.signal: Bristol Myers Squibb is deploying Bunsen and significantly expanding access to Schrödinger's platform across its research organization under a new strategic software agreement covering Bunsen and large-scale chemical-exploration technologies.
